description: llmwiki read-injection: cold-start context once per session, wiki pointers per prompt (silent on unenrolled repos and unconfident turns). Both scripts resolve the engine from their own location, so the plugin cache copy works unmodified. ONE file serves both harnesses: Claude Code auto-discovers hooks/hooks.json, and Codex falls back to the same default path when the manifest declares no `hooks` (codex-rs/core-plugins/src/loader.rs, DEFAULT_HOOKS_CONFIG_FILE) — which it must not, because the public plugin directory's ingestion schema rejects that field. The SessionStart matcher is EMPTY (= every source) rather than a source list: Claude Code evaluates such matchers as an exact string list, not a regex, so an enumerated list silently drops sources added later — it listed startup|resume|clear|compact and stopped matching forked sessions when `fork` was added in Claude Code v2.1.214 (before which forks reported `resume`). The clone install has always written the empty matcher (src/daemon/wire.ts), so this also removes a drift between the two install paths; tests/hook-matcher-drift.test.ts holds them together. CAUTION when adding fields here: Codex parses this file with serde `deny_unknown_fields`, so a key it does not declare is a HARD parse error that takes both hooks down, while Claude Code merely logs and ignores one ('Hook JSON output had unrecognized keys (ignored)'). Only fields BOTH accept belong here — `type`, `command`, `timeout`, `statusMessage`, `matcher`, `additionalContextLimit` (a Codex spill threshold, where 0 means never spill; Claude Code ignores it and caps hook output at a fixed 10,000 characters instead). Claude-only fields like `once`, `if`, `async` and `shell` must NOT be added; note also that `if` is evaluated only on tool events, so putting it on SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit would silently disable the hook.
